reply.thought: Before any payouts, I need to verify the refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds, so I'll start by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches Alpha's reported refunds exactly (orders 260, 263, 265 with the same amounts), so I can proceed. Next I need the list of orders to identify the customers to pay.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report, and the orders map to three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
acme's net balance is 29089. Check: orders 25692 + 20673 = 46365, minus refunds 8294 + 8982 = 17276 gives 29089, which matches. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
birch's net balance is 62075, which matches its orders (32750 + 29325 = 62075) with no refunds. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.

cobalt's net balance is 39438, which matches its orders (33488 + 16853 = 50341) minus refund 265 (10903). All three balances check out against the orders and refunds, so I'll record the first payout, for acme.
acme's payout is recorded. birch's net balance of 62075 matches its orders with no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's balance of 39438 matches its orders minus refund 265 (33488 + 16853 - 10903), so I'll record the last payout.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched its net balance from orders minus refunds. The batch is complete, so I'll finish with the report.
